1.1: Now in the first yere of Cyrus King of Persia (that the word of the Lord, spoken by the mouth of Jeremiah, might be accomplished) the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus King of Persia, and hee made a Proclamation thorowe all his Kingdom, and also by writing, saying,
1.2: Thus saith Cyrus King of Persia, The Lord God of heaven hath given me all the kingdomes of the earth, and he hath commanded me to build him an house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah.
1.3: Who is he among you of all his people with whom his God is? let him goe up to Jerusalem which is in Judah, and buylde the house of the Lord God of Israel: he is the God, which is in Jerusalem.
1.4: And every one that remayneth in any place (where he soiourneth) let the men of his place relieve him with silver and with gold, and with substance, and with cattel, and with a willing offring, for the house of God that is in Jerusalem.
1.5: Then the chief fathers of Judah and Beniamin, and the Priests and Levites rose up, with al them whose spirit God had raysed to goe up, to build the house of the Lord which is in Jerusalem.
1.6: And all they that were about them, strengthened their handes with vessels of silver, with gold, with substance and with cattell, and with precious thinges, besides all that was willingly offred.
1.7: Also the King Cyrus brought forth the vessels of the house of the Lord, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken out of Jerusalem, and had put them in the house of his god.
1.8: Even them did Cyrus King of Persia bring forth by the hand of Mithredath the treasurer, and counted them unto Sheshbazzar the Prince of Judah.
1.9: And this is the nomber of them, thirtie basins of gold, a thousand basins of silver, nine and twentie knives,
1.10: Thirtie boules of gold, and of silver boules of the second sort, four hundreth and tenne, and of other vessels, a thousand.
1.11: All the vessels of gold and silver were five thousand and four hundreth. Sheshbazzar brought up all with them of the captiuitie that came up from Babel to Jerusalem.

2.1: These also are the sonnes of the province, that went up out of the captiuitie (whom Nebuchadnezzar King of Babel had caried away unto Babel) and returned to Jerusalem, and to Judah, every one unto his citie,
2.2: Which came with Zerubbabel, to wit, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, Rehum, Baanah. The number of the men of the people of Israel was,
2.3: The sonnes of Parosh, two thousand, an hudreth seuentie and two:
2.4: The sonnes of Shephatiah, three hundreth, seuentie and two:
2.5: The sonnes of Arah, seven hundreth, and seuentie and five:
2.6: The sonnes of Pahath Moab, of the sonnes of Jeshua and Joab, two thousand, eight hundreth and twelve:
2.7: The sonnes of Elam, a thousand, two hundreth and four and fiftie:
2.8: The sonnes of Zattu, nine hundreth and five and fourtie:
2.9: The sonnes of Zaccai, seven hundreth and threescore:
2.10: The sonnes of Bani, six hundreth and two and fourtie:
2.11: The sonnes of Bebai, six hundreth, and three and twentie:
2.12: The sonnes of Azgad a thousand, two hundreth and two and twentie:
2.13: The sonnes of Adonikam, six hundreth, three score and six:
2.14: The sonnes of Bigvai, two thousand, and six and fiftie:
2.15: The sonnes of Adin, four hundreth and four and fiftie:
2.16: The sonnes of Ater of Hizkiah, ninetie and eight:
2.17: The sonnes of Bezai, three hundreth and three and twentie:
2.18: The sonnes of Jorah, an hudreth and twelve:
2.19: The sonnes of Hashum, two hundreth and three and twentie:
2.20: The sonnes of Gibbar, ninetie and five:
2.21: The sonnes of Beth-lehem, an hundreth and three and twentie:
2.22: The men of Netophah, six and fiftie:
2.23: The men of Anothoth, an hundreth and eight and twentie:
2.24: The sonnes of Azmaveth, two and fourtie:
2.25: The sonnes of Kiriath-arim, of Chephirah, and Beeroth, seven hundreth and three and fourtie:
2.26: The sonnes of Haramah and Gaba, six hundreth, and one and twentie:
2.27: The men of Michmas, an hundreth and two and twentie:
2.28: The sonnes of Beth-el and Ai, two hundreth, and three and twentie:
2.29: The sonnes of Nebo, two and fiftie:
2.30: The sonnes of Magbish, an hundreth and six and fiftie:
2.31: The sonnes of the other Elam, a thousand, and two hundreth, and four and fiftie:
2.32: The sonnes of Harim, three hundreth and twentie:
2.33: The sonnes of Lod-hadid, and Ono, seven hundreth, and five and twentie:
2.34: The sonnes of Jericho, three hundreth and five and fourtie:
2.35: The sonnes of Senaah, three thousand, six hundreth and thirtie.
2.36: The Priests: of the sonnes of Jedaiah of the house of Jeshua, nine hundreth seuentie and three:
2.37: The sonnes of Immer, a thousand and two and fiftie:
2.38: The sonnes of Pashur, a thousand, two hundreth and seven and fourtie:
2.39: The sonnes of Harim, a thousand and seventeen.
2.40: The Levites: the sonnes of Jeshua, and Kadmiel of the sonnes of Hodaviah, seuentie and four.
2.41: The Singers: the sonnes of Asaph, an hundreth and eight and twentie.
2.42: The sonnes of the porters: the sonnes of Shallum, the sonnes of Ater, the sonnes of Talmon, the sonnes of Akkub, the sonnes of Hatita, the sonnes of Shobai: all were an hundreth and nine and thirtie.
2.43: The Nethinims: the sonnes of Ziha, the sonnes of Hasupha, the sonnes of Tabbaoth,
2.44: The sonnes of Keros, the sonnes of Siaha, the sonnes of Padon,
2.45: The sonnes of Lebanah, the sonnes of Hagabah, the sonnes of Akkub,
2.46: The sonnes of Hagab, the sonnes of Shamlai, the sonnes of Hanan,
2.47: The sonnes of Giddel, the sonnes of Gahar, the sonnes of Reaiah,
2.48: The sonnes of Rezin, the sonnes of Nekoda, the sonnes of Gazzam,
2.49: The sonnes of Uzza, the sonnes of Paseah, the sonnes of Besai,
2.50: The sonnes of Asnah, the sonnes of Meunim, the sonnes of Nephusim,
2.51: The sonnes of Bakbuk, the sonnes of Hakupa, the sonnes of Harhur,
2.52: The sonnes of Bazluth, the sonnes of Mehida, the sonnes of Harsha,
2.53: The sonnes of Barcos, the sonnes of Sisara, the sonnes of Thamah,
2.54: The sonnes of Neziah, the sonnes of Hatipha,
2.55: The sonnes of Salomons seruantes: the sonnes of Sotai, the sonnes of Sophereth, the sonnes of Peruda,
2.56: The sonnes of Jaalah, the sonnes of Darkon, the sonnes of Giddel,
2.57: The sonnes of Shephatiah, the sonnes of Hattil, the sonnes of Pochereth Hazzebaim, the sonnes of Ami.
2.58: All the Nethinims, and the sonnes of Salomons servants were three hundreth ninetie and two.
2.59: And these went up from Telmelah, and from Telharsha, Cherub, Addan, and Immer, but they could not discern their fathers house and their seed, whether they were of Israel.
2.60: The sonnes of Delaiah, the sonnes of Tobiah, the sonnes of Nekoda, six hundreth and two and fiftie.
2.61: And of the sonnes of the Priestes, the sonnes of Habaiah, the sonnes of Coz, the sonnes of Barzillai: which took of the daughters of Barzillai the Giliadite to wife, and was called after their name.
2.62: These sought their writing of the genealogies, but they were not found: therefore were they put from the Priesthood.
2.63: And Tirshatha said unto them, that they should not eat of the most holy thing, tell there rose up a Priest with Urim and Thummim.
2.64: The whole Congregation together was two and fourtie thousand, three hundreth and threescore,
2.65: Beside their servants and their maydes: of whom were seven thousand, three hundreth and seven and thirtie: and among them were two hundreth singing men and singing women.
2.66: Their horses were seven hundreth, and six and thirtie: their mules, two hundreth and five and fourtie:
2.67: Their camels four hundreth, and five and thirtie: their asses, six thousand, seven hundreth and twentie.
2.68: And certeine of the chief fathers, when they came to the house of the Lord, which was in Jerusalem, they offred willingly for the house of God, to set it up upon his fundation.
2.69: They gave after their abilitie unto the treasure of the work, even one and threescore thousand drammes of gold, and five thousand pieces of silver, and an hundreth Priests garments.
2.70: So the Priests and the Levites, and a certeine of the people, and the singers, and the porters, and the Nethinims dwelt in their cities, and all Israel in their cities.

3.1: And when the seventh moneth was come, and the children of Israel were in their cities, the people assembled themselves as one man unto Jerusalem.
3.2: Then stood up Jeshua rhe sonne of Jozadak, and his brethren the Priests, and Zerubbabel the sonne of Shealtiel, and his brethren, and builded the altar of the God of Israel, to offer burnt offerings thereon, as it is written in ye Law of Moses the man of God,
3.3: And they set the altar upon his bases (for fear was among them, because of the people of those countreis) therefore they offered burnt offrings thereon unto the Lord, even burnt offrings in the morning, and at even.
3.4: They kept also the feast of the Tabernacles, as it is written, and the burnt offring dayly, by nomber according to the custom day by day,
3.5: And afterward the continual bnrnt offring, both in the new moneths and in all the feast dayes that were consecrate unto the Lord, and in all the oblations willingly offered unto the Lord.
3.6: From the first day of the seventh moneth began they to offer burnt offrings unto the Lord: but the foundation of the Temple of the Lord was not layed.
3.7: They gave money also unto the masons, and to the workemen, and meat and drink, and oyle unto them of Zidon and of Tyrus, to bring them cedar wood from Lebanon to the sea unto Japho, according to the graunt that they had of Cyrus King of Persia.
3.8: And in the second yeere of their coming unto the house of God in Jerusalem in the second moneth began Zerubbabel the sonne of Shealtiel, and Jeshua the sonne of Jozadak, and the remnant of their brethren the Priests and the Levites, and all they that were come out of the captiuitie unto Jerusalem, and appointed the Levites from twentie yeere old and above, to set forward the work of the house of the Lord.
3.9: And Jeshua stood with his sonnes, and his brethren, and Kadmiel with his sonnes, and the sonnes of Judah together to set forward ye workemen in the house of God, and the sonnes of Henadad with their sonnes, and their brethren the Levites.
3.10: And when the builders layed the foundation of the Temple of the Lord, they appoynted the Priestes in their apparel with trumpets, and the Levites the sonnes of Asaph with cymbales, to prayse the Lord, after the ordinance of David King of Israel.
3.11: Thus they sang when they gave prayse, and when they gave thankes unto the Lord, For he is good, for his mercie endureth for ever toward Israel. And all the people shouted with a great shout, when they praysed the Lord, because the foundation of the house of the Lord was layed.
3.12: Many also of the Priests and the Levites and the chief of the fathers, ancient men which had seen the first house, (when the foundation of this house was layed before their eyes) wept with a loud voyce, and many shouted aloud for joy,
3.13: So that the people could not discern the sound of the shout for joy, from the noyse of the weeping of the people: for the people shouted with a loud crie, and the noyse was heard far off.

4.1: But the adversaries of Judah and Beniamin heard, that the children of the captiuitie builded the Temple unto the Lord God of Israel.
4.2: And they came to Zerubbabel, and to the chief fathers, and sayd unto them, We wil build with you: for we seek the Lord your God as ye do, and we have sacrificed unto him since the time of Esar Haddon king of Asshur, which brought us up hither.
4.3: Then Zerubbabel, and Jeshua, and the rest of the chief fathers of Israel, sayde unto them, It is not for you, but for us to buyld the house unto our God: for we our selves together wil buylde it unto the Lord God of Israel, as king Cyrus the king of Persia hath commanded us.
4.4: Wherefore the people of the land discouraged the people of Judah, and troubled them in buylding,
4.5: And they hired counsellers against them, to hinder their devise, all the dayes of Cyrus King of Persia, even until the reign of Darius King of Persia.
4.6: And in the reign of Ahashuerosh (in the beginning of his reign) wrote they an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.
4.7: And in the daies of Artahshashte, Mithredath, Tabeel, and the rest of their companions wrote when it was peace, unto Artahshashte king of Persia, and the writing of the letter was the Aramites writing, and the thing declared was in the language of the Aramites.
4.8: Rehum the chancelour, and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter against Jerusalem to Artahshashte the King, in this sort.
4.9: Then wrote Rehum the chauncelour, and Shimshai the scribe, and their companions Dinaie, and Apharsathcaie, Tarpelaie, Apharsaie, Archeuaie, Bablaie, Shushanchaie, Dehaue, Elmaie,
4.10: And the rest of the people whom the great and noble Asnappar brought over, and set in the cities of Samaria, and other that are beyond the River and Cheeneth.
4.11: This is the copie of the letter that they sent unto King Artahshashte, THY SERVANTS the men beyond the River and Cheeneth, salute thee.
4.12: Be it knowen unto the King that ye Iewes, which came up from thee to us, are come unto Jerusalem (a citie rebellious and wicked) and buylde, and lay the foundations of the walles, and have ioyned the foundations.
4.13: Be it knowen now unto the King, that if this citie be built, and the foundations of the walles layed, they will not give toll, tribute, nor custom: so shalt thou hinder the Kings tribute.
4.14: Now therefore because wee have been brought up in the Kings palace, it was not meet for us to see the Kings dishonour: for this cause have we sent and certified the King,
4.15: That one may search in the book of the Chronicles of thy fathers, and thou shalt find in the book of the Chronicles, and perceive that this citie is rebellious and noysome unto Kings and provinces, and that they have moved sedition of old time, for the which cause this citie was destroyed.
4.16: Wee certifie the King therefore, that if this citie be buylded, and the foundation of the walles layd, by this meanes the portion beyond the River shall not be thine.
4.17: The King sent an answer unto Rehum the Chauncelour, and Shimshai the Scribe, and so the rest of their companions that dwelt in Samaria, and unto the other beyond the River, Shelam and Cheeth.
4.18: The letter which yee sent unto us, hath been openly read before me,
4.19: And I have commanded and they have searched, and found, that this citie of old time hath made insurrection against kings, and hath rebelled, and rebellion hath been committed therein.
4.20: There have been mightie kings also over Jerusalem, which have ruled over all beyond the River, and toll, tribute, and custom was given unto them.
4.21: Make ye now a decree, that those men may cease, and that the citie be not buylt, till I have given another commandement.
4.22: Take heed now that ye fayle not to doe this: why should domage grow to hurt the King?
4.23: When the copie of king Artahshashtes letter was read before Rehum and Shimshai the scribe, and their companions, they went up in all the haste to Jerusalem unto the Iewes, and caused them to cease by force and power.
4.24: Then ceased the work of the house of God, which was in Jerusalem, and did stay unto the second yeere of Darius King of Persia.

5.1: Then Haggai a Prophet and Zechariah the sonne of Iddo a Prophet prophecied unto the Iewes that were in Judah, and Jerusalem, in the name of the God of Israel, even unto them.
5.2: Then Zerubbabel the sonne of Shealtiel, and Jeshua the sonne of Jozadak arose, and began to build the house of God at Jerusalem, and with them were the Prophetes of God, which helped them.
5.3: At the same time came to them Tatnai, which was captain beyond the River, and Shether-boznai and their companions, and sayd thus unto them, Who hath given you commandement to buylde this house, and to lay the foundations of these walles?
5.4: Then sayde we unto them after this maner, What are the names of the men that buylde this buylding?
5.5: But the eye of their God was upon the Elders of the Iewes, that they could not cause them to cease, till the matter came to Darius: and then they answered by letters thereunto.
5.6: The copie of the letter, that Tatnai captain beyond the River, and Shether-boznai and his companions, Apharsechaie, (which were beyond the River) sent unto King Darius.
5.7: They sent a letter unto him, wherein it was written thus, Unto Darius the king, all peace.
5.8: Be it knowen unto the King, that we went into the province of Judea, to the house of the great God, which is builded with great stones, and beames are layde in the walles, and this work is wrought speedily, and prospereth in their hands.
5.9: Then asked we those Elders, and sayd unto them thus, Who hath given you commandement to buylde this house, and to lay the foundation of these walles?
5.10: We asked their names also, that we might certifie thee, and that we might write the names of the men that were their rulers.
5.11: But they answered us thus, and sayd, We are the servants of the God of heaven and earth, and buylde the house that was buylt of old and many yeeres ago, which a great King of Israel builded, and founded it.
5.12: But after that our fathers had provoked the God of heaven unto wrath, he gave them over into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar King of Babel the Caldean, and he destroyed this house, and caryed the people away captive unto Babel.
5.13: But in the first yere of Cyrus King of Babel, King Cyrus made a decree to buylde this house of God.
5.14: And the vessels of gold and silver of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar took out of the Temple, that was in Jerusalem, and brought them into the Temple of Babel, those did Cyrus the king take out of the Temple of Babel, and they gave them unto one Sheshbazzar by his name, whom he had made captain.
5.15: And he sayde unto him, Take these vessels and goe thy way, and put them in the Temple that is in Jerusalem, and let the house of God be buylt in his place.
5.16: Then came the same Sheshbazzar and layde the foundation of the house of God, which is in Jerusalem, and since that time even until now, hath it been in buylding, yet is it not finished.
5.17: Now therefore if it please the King, let there be search made in the house of the Kings treasures, which is there in Babel, whether a decree hath been made by King Cyrus, to build this house of God in Jerusalem, and let the King send his mind concerning this.

6.1: Then King Darius gave commandement, and they made search in the librarie of the treasures, which were there layd up in Babel.
6.2: And there was found in a coffer (in the palace that was in the province of the Medes) a volume, and therein was it thus written, as a memorial,
6.3: IN THE FIRST yeere of King Cyrus, King Cyrus made a decree for the house of God in Jerusalem, Let the house be buylt, even the place where they offred sacrifices, and let the walles thereof be ioyned together: let the height thereof be three score cubites, and the breadth thereof three score cubites,
6.4: Three orders of great stones, and one order of timber, and let the expenses be given of the Kings house.
6.5: And also let them render the vessels of the house of God (of gold and silver, which Nebuchadnezzar took out of the Temple, which was in Jerusalem, and brought unto Babel) and let him goe unto the Temple that is in Jerusalem to his place, and put them in the house of God.
6.6: Therefore Tatnai captain beyond the River, and Shethar Boznai, (and their companions Apharsecaie, which are beyond the River) be ye far from thence.
6.7: Suffer ye the work of this house of God, that the captain of the Iewes and the Elders of the Iewes may buylde this house of God in his place.
6.8: For I have given a commandement what ye shall doe to the Elders of these Iewes, for the buylding of this house of God, that of the reuenues of the King, which is of the tribute beyond the River, there be incontinently expenses given unto these men that they cease not.
6.9: And that which they shall have need of, let it be given unto them day by day, whether it be yong bullockes, or rammes, or lambes for the burnt offrings of the God of heaven, wheat, salt, wine, and oyle, according to the appoyntment of the Priestes that are in Jerusalem, that there bee no fault,
6.10: That they may have to offer sweet odours unto the God of heaven, and pray for the Kings life, and for his sonnes.
6.11: And I have made a decree, that whosoever shall alter this sentence, the wood shall be pulled down from his house, and shall be set up, and he shalbe hanged thereon, and his house shalbe made a dunghill for this.
6.12: And the God that hath caused his Name to dwell there, destroy all Kings and people that put to their hand to alter, and to destroy this house of God, which is in Jerusalem. I Darius have made a decree, let it be done with speed.
6.13: Then Tatnai the captain beyond the River, and Shethar Boznai and their companions, according to that which Darius had sent, so they did speedily.
6.14: So the Elders of the Iewes builded, and they prospered by the prophecying of Haggai the Prophet, and Zechariah the sonne of Iddo, and they buylded and finished it, by the appoyntment of the God of Israel, and by the commandement of Cyrus and Darius, and Artahshashte king of Persia.
6.15: And this house was finished the third day of the moneth Adar, which was the sixt yeere of the reign of King Darius.
6.16: And the children of Israel, the Priestes, and the Levites, and the residue of the children of the captiuitie kept the dedication of this house of God with joy,
6.17: And offred at the dedication of this house of God an hundreth bullockes, two hundreth rams, four hundreth lambes, and twelve goates, for the sinne of all Israel, according to the nomber of the tribes of Israel.
6.18: And they set the Priests in their order, and the Levites in their courses over the service of God in Jerusalem, as it is written in the book of Moses.
6.19: And the childre of the captiuitie kept the Passeouer on ye fourtenth day of the first moneth.
6.20: (For the Priests and the Levites were purified altogether) and they killed the Passeouer for all the children of the captiuitie, and for their brethren the Priests, and for themselves.
6.21: So the children of Israel which were come again out of captiuitie, and all such as had separated themselves unto them, from the filthines of the Heathen of the land, to seek the Lord God of Israel, did eat,
6.22: And they kept ye feast of vnleauened bread seven dayes with joy: for the Lord had made them glad, and turned the heart of the King of Asshur unto them, to incourage them in the work of the house of God, even the God of Israel.

7.1: Now after these things, in the reign of Artahshashte King of Persia, was Ezra the sonne of Seraiah, the sonne of Azariah, the sonne of Hilkiah,
7.2: The sonne of Shallum, the sonne of Zadok, the sonne of Ahitub,
7.3: The sonne of Amariah, the sonne of Azariah, the sonne of Meraioth,
7.4: The sonne of Zeraiah, the sonne of Uzzi, the sonne of Bukki,
7.5: The sonne of Abishua, the sonne of Phinehas, the sonne of Eleazar, the sonne of Aaron, the chief Priest.
7.6: This Ezra came up from Babel, and was a Scribe prompt in the Law of Moses, which the Lord God of Israel had given, and the King gave him all his request according to the hand of the Lord his God which was upon him.
7.7: And there went up certain of the children of Israel, and of the Priests, and the Levites, and the singers, and the porters, and the Nethinims unto Jerusalem, in the seventh yere of King Artahshashte.
7.8: And hee came to Jerusalem in the fift moneth, which was in the seventh yeere of the King.
7.9: For upon the first day of the first moneth began he to goe up from Babel, and on the first day of the fift moneth came he to Jerusalem, according to the good hand of his God that was upon him.
7.10: For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the Law of the Lord, and to doe it, and to teach the precepts and iudgements in Israel.
7.11: And this is the copie of the letter that King Artahshashte gave unto Ezra the Priest and scribe, even a writer of the words of the commadements of ye Lord, and of his statutes over Israel.
7.12: ARTAHSHASHTE King of Kings to Ezra the Priest and perfite scribe of the Law of the God of heaven, and to Cheeneth.
7.13: I have given commandement, that every one, that is willing in my kingdom of the people of Israel, and of the Priestes, and Levites to goe to Jerusalem with thee, shall goe.
7.14: Therefore art thou sent of the King and his seven counsellers, to enquire in Judah and Jerusalem, according to the law of thy God, which is in thine hand,
7.15: And to carry the silver and the gold, which the King and his cousellers willingly offer unto the God of Israel (whose habitation is in Jerusalem)
7.16: And all the silver and gold that thou canst find in all the province of Babel, with the free offring of the people, and that which the Priestes offer willingly to the house of their God which is in Jerusalem,
7.17: That thou mayest bye speedily with this silver, bullocks, rammes, lambes, with their meat offrings and their drink offrings: and thou shalt offer them upon the altar of the house of your God, which is in Jerusalem.
7.18: And whatsoever it pleaseth thee and thy brethren to do with the rest of the silver, and gold, doe ye it according to the will of your God.
7.19: And the vessels that are given thee for the service of the house of thy God, those deliver thou before God in Jerusalem.
7.20: And the residue that shall be needeful for the house of thy God, which shall be meet for thee to bestow, thou shalt bestow it out of the Kings treasure house,
7.21: And I King Artahshashte have given commandemet to all the treasurers which are beyond the River, that whatsoever Ezra the Priest and Scribe of the Law of the God of heaven shall require of you, that it be done incontinently,
7.22: Unto an hundreth talents of silver, unto an hundreth measures of wheat, and unto an hundreth baths of wine, and unto an hundreth baths of oyle, and salt without writing.
7.23: Whatsoever is by the commandement of the God of heaven, let it be done speedily for the house of the God of heaven: for why should he be wroth against the realm of the King, and his children?
7.24: And we certifie you, that upon any of the Priestes, Levites, singers, porters, Nethinims, or Ministers in this house of God, there shall no gouernour lay upon them toll, tribute nor custom.
7.25: And thou Ezra (after the wisedome of thy God, that is in thine hand) set judges and arbiters, which may judge all the people that is beyond the River, even all that know the Law of thy God, and teach ye them that know it not.
7.26: And whosoever will not doe the Law of thy God, and the Kings law, let him have iudgement without delay, whether it be unto death, or to banishment, or to confiscation of goods, or to imprisonment.
7.27: Blessed be the Lord God of our fathers, which so hath put in the Kings heart, to beautifie the house of the Lord that is in Jerusalem,
7.28: And hath enclined mercy toward me, before the King and his counsellers, and before all the Kings mightie Princes: and I was comforted by the hand of the Lord my God which was upon me, and I gathered the chief of Israel to goe up with me.

8.1: These are now the chief fathers of them, and the genealogie of them that came up with mee from Babel, in the reign of King Artahshashte.
8.2: Of the sonnes of Phinehas, Gershom: of the sonnes of Ithamar, Daniel: of the sonnes of David, Hattush:
8.3: Of the sonnes of Shechaniah, of the sonnes of Pharosh, Zechariah, and with him the count of the males, an hundreth and fiftie.
8.4: Of the sonnes of Pahath Moab, Elihoenai, the sonne of Zerahiah, and with him two hundreth males.
8.5: Of the sonnes of Shechaniah, the sonne of Jahaziel, and with him three hundreth males.
8.6: And of the sonnes of Adin, Ebed the sonne of Jonathan, and with him fiftie males.
8.7: And of the sonnes of Elam, Jeshaiah the sonne of Athaliah, and with him seuentie males.
8.8: And of the sonnes of Shephatiah, Zebadiah the sonne of Michael, and with him fourescore males.
8.9: Of the sonnes of Joab, Obadiah the sonne of Jehiel, and with him two hundreth and eighteen males.
8.10: And of the sonnes of Shelomith the sonne of Josiphiah, and with him an hundreth and threescore males.
8.11: And of the sonnes of Bebai, Zechariah the sonne of Bebai, and with him eight and twentie males.
8.12: And of the sonnes of Azgad, Johanan the sonne of Hakkatan, and with him an hundreth and ten males.
8.13: And of the sonnes of Adonikam, that were the last, whose names are these: Eliphelet, Jehiel and Shemaiah, and with them three score males.
8.14: And of the sonnes of Bigvai, Uthai, and Zabbud, and with them seuentie males.
8.15: And I gathered them to the River that goeth toward Ahava, and there abode we three dayes: then I viewed the people, and the Priests, and found there none of the sonnes of Levi.
8.16: Therefore sent I to Eliezer, to Ariel, to Shemeiah, and to Elnathan, and to Jarib, and to Elnathan, and to Nathan, and to Zechariah, and to Meshullam the chief, and to Joiarib and to Elnathan, men of understanding,
8.17: And I gave them commandement, to Iddo the chiefest at the place of Casiphia, and I told them the words that they should speak to Iddo, and to his brethren the Nethinims at the place of Casiphia, that they should cause the ministers of the house of our God to come unto us.
8.18: So by the good hand of our God which was upon us, they brought us a man of understanding of the sonnes of Mahali the sonne of Levi the sonne of Israel, and Sherebiah with his sonnes and his brethren, even eighteen.
8.19: Also Hashabiah, and with him Jeshaiah of the sonnes of Merari, with his brethren, and their sonnes twentie.
8.20: And of the Nethinims, whom David had set, and the Princes for the service of the Levites, two hundreth and twentie of the Nethinims, which all were named by name.
8.21: And there at the River, by Ahava, I proclaimed a fast, that we might humble our selves before our God, and seek of him a right way for us, and for our children, and for all our substance.
8.22: For I was ashamed to require of the King an armie and horsemen, to help us against the enemie in the way, because we had spoken to the King, saying, The hand of our God is upon all them that seek him in goodness, but his power and his wrath is against all them that forsake him.
8.23: So we fasted, aud besought our God for this: and he was intreated of us.
8.24: Then I separated twelve of the chief of the Priests, Sherebiah, and Hashabiah, and ten of their brethren with them,
8.25: And weighed them the silver and the gold, and the vessels, even the offring of ye house of our God, which the King and his counselers, and his Princes, and all Israel that were present had offred.
8.26: And I weighed unto their hand six hundreth and fiftie talents of silver, and in silver vessel, an hundreth talents, and in gold, an hundreth talents:
8.27: And twentie basins of gold, of a thousand drammes, and two vessels of shining brass very good, and precious as gold.
8.28: And I said unto them, Ye are consecrate unto the Lord, and the vessels are consecrate, and the gold and the silver are freely offred unto the Lord God of your fathers.
8.29: Watch ye, and keep them until ye weigh them before the chief Priestes and the Levites, and the chief fathers of Israel in Jerusalem in the chambers of the house of the Lord.
8.30: So the Priests and the Levites received the weight of the silver and of the gold, and of the vessels to bring them to Jerusalem, unto the house of our God.
8.31: Then we departed from the River of Ahauah on the twelft day of the first moneth, to go unto Jerusalem, and the hand of our God was upon us, and delivered us from the hand of the enemie, and of such as layde wait by the way.
8.32: And we came to Jerusalem, and abode there three dayes.
8.33: And on ye fourth day was the silver weighed, and the gold and the vessell in the house of our God by the hand of Meremoth the sonne of Uriah the Priest, and with him was Eleazar the sonne of Phinehas, and with them was Jozabad the sonne of Jeshua, and Noadiah the sonne of Binnui the Levites,
8.34: By number and by weight of every one, and all the weight was written at the same time.
8.35: Also the children of the captiuitie, which were come out of captiuitie, offred burnt offrings unto the God of Israel, twelve bullockes for all Israel, ninetie and six rammes, seuentie and seven lambes, and twelve hee goates for sinne: all was a burnt offring of the Lord.
8.36: And they delivered the Kings commission unto the Kings officers, and to the captaines beyond the River: and they promoted the people, and the house of God.

9.1: When as these things were done, the rulers came to me, saying, The people of Israel, and the Priestes, and the Levites are not separated from the people of the lands (as touching their abominations) to wit, of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians, and the Amorites.
9.2: For they have taken their daughters to theselues, and to their sonnes, and they have mixed the holy seed with the people of the landes, and the hand of the princes and rulers hath been chief in this trespass.
9.3: But when I heard this saying, I rent my clothes and my garment, and pluckt off the hear of mine head, and of my beard, and sat down astonied.
9.4: And there assembled unto me all that feared the words of the God of Israel, because of the transgression of them of the captiuitie. And I sat down astonied until the evening sacrifice.
9.5: And at the evening sacrifice I arose up from mine heaviness, and when I had rent my clothes and my garment, I fell upon my knees, and spred out mine hands unto the Lord my God,
9.6: And said, O my God, I am confounded and ashamed, to lift up mine eyes unto thee my God: for our iniquities are increased over our head, and our trespass is growen up unto the heaven.
9.7: From the dayes of our fathers have we bin in a great trespass unto this day, and for our iniquities have we, our Kings, and our Priestes been delivered into the hand of the kings of the lands, unto the sword, into captiuitie, into a spoyle, and into confusion of face, as appeareth this day.
9.8: And now for a litle space grace hath been shewed from the Lord our God, in causing a remnant to escape, and in giving us a nayle in his holy place, that our God may light our eyes, and give us a litle reviving in our seruitude.
9.9: For though we were bondmen, yet our God hath not forsaken us in our bondage, but hath enclined mercy unto us in the sight of the Kings of Persia, to give us life, and to erect the house of our God, and to redresse the places thereof, and to give us a wall in Judah and in Jerusalem.
9.10: And now, our God, what shall we say after this? for we have forsaken thy commandements,
9.11: Which thou hast commanded by thy servants the Prophets, saying, The land whereunto ye go to possess it, is an vncleane land, because of the filthines of the people of the lands, which by their abominations, and by their vncleannes have filled it from corner to corner.
9.12: Now therfore shall ye not give your daughters unto their sonnes, neither shall ye take their daughters unto your sonnes, nor seek their peace nor wealth for ever, that yee may be strong and eat the goodnes of the land, and leave it for an inheritance to your sonnes for ever.
9.13: And after all that is come upon us for our evil deedes, and for our great trespasses, (seeing that thou our God hast stayed us from being beneath for our iniquities, and hast given us such deliverance)
9.14: Should we return to break thy commadements, and ioyne in affinitie with the people of such abominations? wouldest not thou be angrie toward us till thou haddest consumed us, so that there should be no remnant nor any escaping?
9.15: O Lord God of Israel, thou art just, for we have been reserved to escape, as appeareth this day: behold, we are before thee in our trespass: therfore we canot stand before thee because of it.

10.1: Whiles Ezra prayed thus, and confessed himself weeping, and falling down before the house of God, there assembled unto him of Israel a very great Congregation of men and women and children: for the people wept with a great lamentation.
10.2: Then Shechaniah the sonne of Jehiel one of the sonnes of Elam answered, and sayd to Ezra, We have trespassed against our God, and have taken strange wives of the people of the land, yet now there is hope in Israel concerning this.
10.3: Now therfore let us make a covenant with our God, to put away all the wives (and such as are borne of them) according to the counsel of the Lord, and of those that fear the commandements of our God, and let it be done according to the Law.
10.4: Arise: for the matter belogeth unto thee: we also wil be with thee: be of comfort and do it.
10.5: Then arose Ezra, and caused the chief Priestes, the Levites, and all Israel, to swear that they would doe according to this word. So they sware.
10.6: And Ezra rose up from before the house of God, and went into the chamber of Johanan the sonne of Eliashib: he went even thither, but he did eat neither bread, nor drunk water: for he mourned, because of the transgression of them of the captiuitie.
10.7: And they caused a proclamation to goe throughout Judah and Jerusalem, unto all them of the captiuitie, that they should assemble themselves unto Jerusalem.
10.8: And whosoever would not come within three dayes according to the counsel of the Princes and Elders, all his substance should be forfait, and he should be separate from the Congregation of them of the captiuitie.
10.9: Then all the men of Judah and Beniamin assembled theselues unto Jerusalem within three dayes, which was the twentieth day of the ninth moneth, and all the people sat in the street of the house of God, trembling for this matter, and for the rain.
10.10: And Ezra the Priest stood up, and said unto them, Ye have transgressed, and have taken strange wives, to increase the trespass of Israel.
10.11: Now therefore give praise unto the Lord God of your fathers, and do his will, and separate your selves from the people of the land, and from the strange wives.
10.12: And all the Congregation answered, and sayd with a loud voyce, So will we do according to thy wordes unto us.
10.13: But the people are many, and it is a raynie weather, and we are not able to stand without, neither is it the work of one day or two: for we are many that have offended in this thing.
10.14: Let our rulers stand therefore before all the Congregation, and let all them which have taken strange wives in our cities, come at the time appoynted, and with them the Elders of every citie and the Judges thereof, til the fierce wrath of our God for this matter turn away from us.
10.15: Then were appoynted Jonathan the sonne of Asah-el, and Jahaziah the sonne of Tikvah over this matter, and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levites helped them.
10.16: And they of the captiuitie did so, and departed, even Ezra the Priest, and the men that were chief fathers to the familie of their fathers by name, and sat down in the first day of the tenth moneth to examine the matter.
10.17: And until the first day of the first moneth they were finishing the business with al the men that had taken strange wives.
10.18: And of the sonnes of the Priests there were men found, that had taken strange wives, to wit, of the sonnes of Jeshua, the sonne of Jozadak, and of his brethren, Maaseiah, Aeliezer, and Jarib and Gedaliah.
10.19: And they gave their hads, that they would put away their wives, and they that had trespassed, gave a ramme for their trespass.
10.20: And of the sonnes of Immer, Honani, and Zebadiah.
10.21: And of the sonnes of Harim, Maaseiah, and Eliiah, and Shemaiah, and Jehiel, and Uzziah.
10.22: And of ye sonnes of Pashur, Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethaneel, Jozabad, and Elasah.
10.23: And of the Levites, Jozabad and Shimei, and Kelaiah, (which is Kelitah) Pethahiah, Judah and Eliezer.
10.24: And of the singers, Eliashib. And of the porters, Shallum, and Telem, and Uri.
10.25: And of Israel: of the sonnes of Parosh, Ramiah, and Jesiah, and Malchiah, and Miamin, and Eleazar, and Malchiiah, and Benaiah.
10.26: And of the sonnes of Elam, Mattaniah, Zechariah, and Jehiel, and Abdi, and Jeremoth, and Eliah.
10.27: And of the sonnes of Zattu, Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, and Jerimoth, and Zabad, and Aziza.
10.28: And of the sonnes of Bebai, Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, Athlai.
10.29: And of the sonnes of Bani, Meshullam, Malluch, and Adaiah, Jashub, and Sheal, Ieramoth.
10.30: And of the sonnes of Pahath Moab, Adna, and Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezaleel, and Binnui, and Manasseh.
10.31: And of the sonnes of Harim, Eliezer, Ishiiah, Malchiah, Shemaiah, Shimeon,
10.33: Of the sonnes of Hashum, Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, Shimei.
10.34: Of the sonnes of Bani, Maadai, Amram, and Uel,
10.39: And Shelemiah, and Nathan, and Adaiah,
10.43: Of the sonnes of Nebo, Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jadau, and Joel, Benaiah.
10.44: All these had taken strange wives: and among them were women that had children.

15:1:1: That is, moved him, and gave him heart.
After that he and Darius had won Babylon.
Who promised them deliverance after that seventy years were past, Jer. 25:12.
15:1:2: For he was chief Monarch, and had many nations under his dominion, which this heathen king confesseth to have received of the living God.
15:1:4: If any through poverty were not able to return, the king’s commission was that he should be furnished with necessaries.
Which they themselves should send toward the reparation of the Temple.
15:1:6: The Babylonians and Chaldeans gave them these presents: thus rather than the children of God should want for their necessities, he would stir up the heart of the very infidels to help them.
15:1:8: So the Chaldeans called Zerubbabel who was the chief governor, so that the preeminence still remained in the house of David.
15:1:9: Which served to kill the beasts that were offered in sacrifice.
15:1:11: With the Jews that had been kept captives in Babylon.
15:2:1: Meaning, Judea, which was a province, that is, a country which was in subjection.
15:2:2: Zerubbabel was chief captain, and Jeshua the high Priest: but Nehemiah a man of great authority went not now, but came after 64 years.
This was not that Mordecai which was Esther’s kinsman.
15:2:6: Or, of the Duke of Moab.
15:2:16: Which were of the posterity of Hezekiah.
15:2:21: That is, inhabitants, for so this word (some) signifieth when it is joined with the names of places.
15:2:36: Before he hath declared the two tribes of Judah and Benjamin, and now cometh to the tribe of Levi, and beginneth at the Priests.
15:2:43: So called, because they were given to the Temple, to cut wood and bear water for the use of the sacrifices, and came of the Gibeonites, which were appointed to this use by Joshua, Josh. 9:23.
15:2:55: Which came of them that Solomon had appointed for the work of the Temple.
15:2:61: Of him is made mention, 2 Sam. 17:27 and 19:31, and because the Priest’s office was had in contempt, these would have changed their estate by their name, and so by God’s just judgment lost both the estimation of the world and the dignity of their office.
15:2:63: This is a Chaldean name, and signifieth him that hath authority over others.
15:2:69: Which are called, mina, and contain a piece two marks: so 50,000 minas make 55,000 franks, which mount to of our money 69,666 pounds, 13 shillings 4 pence so that the whole sum was 94,493 pounds, 6 shillings, 8 pence.

Which mount to of our money, 24,826 pounds, 13 shillings and 4 pence, esteeming the French crown at 6 shillings and 4 pence for the dram is the eighth part of an ounce, and the ounce the eighth part of a mark.
15:3:1: Called Tishri which answereth to part of September and part of October.
15:3:2: Meaning, nephew: for he was the son of Pedaiah, read 1 Chron. 3:19.
15:3:3: In the place where Solomon had placed it.
15:3:5: That is, after the feast of Tabernacles.
15:3:8: Which month contained part of April and part of May: for in the mean season they had provided for things necessary for the work.
15:3:9: They gave them exhortations, and encouraged every man forward in the work.
15:3:12: Because they saw that it was nothing so glorious as that Temple, which Solomon had built, notwithstanding Aggeus comforteth them, and prophesieth that it shall be more beautiful than the first: meaning the spiritual Temple, which are the members of Christ’s body.
15:4:1: Meaning, the inhabitants of Samaria, whom the king of Assyria had placed in the stead of the ten tribes, 2 Kings 17:24 and 19:37. These professed God, but worshipped idols also, and therefore were the greatest enemies to the true servants of God.
15:4:3: For they perceived what their pretence was, to wit, to erect idolatry instead of true religion.
15:4:5: They bribed the governors under the king to hinder their work: Thus they that halt, cannot abide that God should be purely served.
15:4:6: He was also called Artaxerxes, which is a Persian name, some think it was Cambises Cyrus’ son, or Darius, as verse 5.
15:4:7: Called Artaxerxes, which signifieth in the Persian tongue, an excellent warrior.
15:4:9: These were certain people which the Assyrians placed in Samaria instead of the ten tribes.
15:4:10: Which were a certain people that envied the Jews.
Some think it was Sennacherib, but rather Shalmaneser.
To wit, Euphrates: and he meaneth in respect of Babel that they dwelt beyond it.
15:4:13: Meaning, the gifts that are wont to be given to kings when they pass by any country.
15:4:14: Hebrew, in the Chaldea, we have eaten the salt of the palace.
15:4:17: Some read for Shalom, salutation or greeting.
15:4:24: Not altogether for the Prophets exhorted them to continue, but they used less diligence because of the troubles.
15:5:2: Which encouraged them to go forward, and accused them that they were more careful to build their own houses, than zealous to build the Temple of God.
15:5:4: That is, the enemies asked this, as verse 10.
15:5:5: His favor and the spirit of strength.
15:5:17: Meaning, in the library, or places where lay the register or records of times.
15:6:2: Wherein were the acts of the kings of the Medes and Persians.
15:6:5: Meaning, Zerubbabel to whom he giveth charge.
15:6:6: Meddle not with them neither hinder them.
15:6:12: Who hath appointed that place to have his Name called upon there.
15:6:14: Whom God stirs up to assure them that he would give their work good success.
15:6:15: And the two and fortieth year after their first return.
This is the twelfth month and containeth part of February and part of March.
15:6:21: Which were of the heathen, and forsaked their idolatry to worship the true God.
15:6:22: Meaning, Darius who was king of the Medes, Persians, and Assyrians.
15:7:1: The Hebrews write, that divers of the kings of Persia were called by this name, as Pharaoh was a common name to the kings of Egypt, and Caesar to the Emperors Roman.
15:7:5: Ezra deduceth his kindred, till he cometh to Aaron, to prove that he came of him.
15:7:6: He showeth here what a Scribe is, who had charge to write the Law and to expound it, whom Mark calleth a Scribe, Mark 12:28, Matthew and Luke called him a Lawyer or doctor of the Law, Matt. 22:35; Luke 10:25.
15:7:8: That contained part of July, and part of August.
15:7:12: Some take this for the name of a people, some for time or continuance, meaning that the king wished him long life.
15:7:13: Which remained as yet in Babylon and had not returned with Zerubbabel.
15:7:14: To examine who lived according to the Law.
15:7:18: As ye know best may serve to God’s glory.
15:7:21: Which was the river Euphrates, and they were beyond it in respect of Babylon.
15:7:23: This declareth that the fear of God’s judgments causeth him to use this liberality, and not the love that he bare to God’s glory: or affection to his people.
15:7:25: He gave Ezra full authority to restore all things according to the word of God, and to punish them that resisted, and would not obey.
15:7:27: Thus Ezra gave God thanks for that he gave him so good success in his affairs by reason of the king.
15:8:13: That came to go with Ezra.
15:8:15: To that place of Euphrates, where Ahava the river entereth into it.
15:8:17: Hebrew, put words in their mouth.
He was the chiefest that taught there the Law of God unto the Levites.
15:8:21: He showeth that the end of fasting, is to humble the body to the spirit, which must proceed of the heart lively touched, or else it is but hypocrisy.
15:8:22: He thought it better to commit himself to the protection of God, than by seeking these ordinary means to give occasion to others to think that he did doubt of God’s power.
15:8:31: This declared that their journey was full of danger, and yet God delivered them according to their prayer.
15:8:33: This was a token of a good conscience and of his integrity, that he would have witnesses of his fidelity.
15:9:1: From the time they came home under Zerubbabel until the coming of Ezra, they had degenerated contrary to the Law of God, and married where it was not lawful, Deut. 7:3.
15:9:2: That is, the governors are the chief beginners hereof.
15:9:3: As one doubting whether God would continue his benefits towards us, or else destroy this which he had begun.
15:9:6: They so exceed that they cannot grow greater.
That is, we are drowned in sin.
15:9:8: In giving us a resting place. It is a similitude taken of them that remain still in a place, which smite nails to hang things upon, Isa. 22:23.
15:9:13: Hast not utterly cast us down and destroyed us for our sins, Deut. 28:13.
15:9:15: He showeth that God is just in punishing his people, and yet merciful in reserving a residue in whom he showeth favor.
15:10:1: He confessed his sins, and the sins of the people.
15:10:2: Meaning, that God would receive them to mercy.
15:10:3: Which are strangers and married contrary to the Law of God.
15:10:4: Because God hath given thee authority and learning to persuade the people herein, and to command them.
15:10:7: Hebrew, the sons of the captivity.
15:10:9: For the season was given to rain and so the weather was more sharp and cold, and also their conscience touched them.
Which contained part of November and part of December.
15:10:10: Ye have laid one sin upon another.
15:10:14: Let them be appointed to examine this matter.
15:10:16: They went to the chief cities to sit on this matter which was three months in finishing.
15:10:19: As a token that they would keep promise and do it.
15:10:25: Meaning, of the common people: for before he spake of the Priests and Levites.
15:10:44: Which also were made illegitimate because the marriage was unlawful.
